guide.line: In March 1868 a twenty-nine-year-old Scot landed in San Francisco, asked a passer-by for the quickest way out of the city, and set off east on foot toward a wall of mountains he had never seen.
guide.copy_md_sentence: In March 1868 a twenty-nine-year-old Scot landed in San Francisco, asked a passer-by for the quickest way out of the city, and set off east on foot toward a wall of mountains he had never seen.

guide.line: John Muir was born in Dunbar, Scotland, on 21 April 1838, and attended the local schools until he was eleven.
guide.copy_md_sentence: John Muir was born in Dunbar, Scotland, on 21 April 1838, and attended the local schools until he was eleven.

guide.line: In 1849 his family emigrated to the United States and settled on Wisconsin farmland.
guide.copy_md_sentence: In 1849 his family emigrated to the United States and settled on Wisconsin farmland — first at Fountain Lake, then at Hickory Hill Farm near Portage.

guide.line: In 1867, working in a carriage shop in Indianapolis, a file slipped and blinded him in one eye.
guide.copy_md_sentence: In 1867, working in a carriage shop in Indianapolis, a file slipped and blinded him in one eye; the other went dark in sympathy, and he lay in a shuttered room for weeks.

guide.line: When his sight came back he resolved to give up machinery and devote himself to the natural world.
guide.copy_md_sentence: When his sight came back he resolved to give up machinery and devote himself to the natural world, and set out to walk roughly a thousand miles from Indianapolis to the Gulf of Mexico.

guide.line: He walked out across the San Joaquin Valley and up into the Sierra Nevada, which he named "the Range of Light."
guide.copy_md_sentence: He walked out across the San Joaquin Valley and up into the Sierra Nevada, which he named "the Range of Light."

guide.line: Writing, for Muir, was a way of defending what he loved.

guide.line: In 1890, after a campaign Muir fought alongside the editor Robert Underwood Johnson, an act of Congress created Yosemite National Park.
guide.copy_md_sentence: In 1890, after a campaign Muir fought alongside the editor Robert Underwood Johnson, an act of Congress created Yosemite National Park; the National Park Service dates it precisely to 1 October 1890.

guide.line: Two years later Muir and a circle of allies founded the Sierra Club "to do something for wildness and make the mountains glad."
guide.copy_md_sentence: Two years later Muir and a circle of allies founded the Sierra Club "to do something for wildness and make the mountains glad."

guide.line: President Theodore Roosevelt came west in 1903 to see Yosemite with Muir himself.
guide.copy_md_sentence: His 1901 book *Our National Parks* caught the attention of President Theodore Roosevelt, who came west in 1903 to see Yosemite with Muir himself.

guide.line: The two slipped away from the official party into the back country for several days; Roosevelt went home and threw the weight of the presidency behind protecting the nation's forests, parks and monuments.
guide.copy_md_sentence: The two slipped away from the official party into the back country for several days; Roosevelt went home and threw the weight of the presidency behind protecting the nation's forests, parks and monuments.
Its opening lines are the plainest statement Muir ever wrote of why wild country was worth a nation's trouble.

guide.line: Thousands of tired, nerve-shaken, over-civilized people are beginning to find out that going to the mountains is going home; that wildness is a necessity.
